comments.text_zh: 取决于你有多少时间，我首先推荐看 Karpathy 的“深入解析 LLM”视频（[VIDEO]）。它有 3.5 小时，但会让你对这些东西如何工作产生大量直觉理解，并且很可能帮你节省很多时间。纯粹从技术角度来说，事情其实没那么难。我建议你在所有主要提供商那里开一个 API 账号（因为每个前沿 LLM 显然都有自己的强项和弱项），然后开始用自己的数据做实验。你第一次拿到 API 响应时的感觉会让你继续下去！:) 话虽如此，有个提醒：LLM 确实会时不时产生幻觉。如果你的数据需要准确性，绝对不要“把所有东西都扔给 LLM 让它们干活”，但我相信你会通过试错搞明白的。祝你好运！
comments.text: Depending on how much time you have, the first thing I would recommend is to watch Karpathy's 'deep dive into LLMs' video ( [VIDEO] ). It is 3.5 hours but it will give you so much instinctive understanding of how these things work and will likely save you a lot of time. Purely from a technical standpoint, things aren't that difficult really. I'd recommend get yourself an API account with all major providers (because each frontier LLM evidently has their own strengths and weaknesses) and start experimenting with your data. The feeling you'll get when you first get an API response will keep you going! :) Having said that, a caveat is, LLMs do hallucinate from time to time. If your data needs accuracy, definitely don't do the "throw everything at LLMs and let them do the work" but I'm sure you'll figure it out from trial and error. Good luck!

comments.author: wzdd
comments.story_title: Tracing the thoughts of a large language model
comments.why_zh: 关于基础训练与后训练的好入门讲解。
comments.quote_zh: Karpathy 有一个很好的入门视频讲这个。
comments.text_zh: > 模型仍然在 _逐 token 生成_ 回复，但它们选择 token 时 _并不是_ 基于在每个 token 处最大化概率的那些 token。这也不是基础训练的工作方式。在基础训练中，损失是在给定上下文的条件下选择的，而上下文可以非常巨大。它从来都不只是关于前一个 token，而是关于上下文中一整个回复。上下文可以是一整首诗、一部戏剧、一个编程题目的完整解答，等等等等。所以你会预期从基础训练模型身上看到同样类型的（表面上的）更高层次规划，事实上你确实能看到，而且很容易验证：从 HF 或类似地方下载一个基础模型，提示它补全一首诗就行。基础模型和智能体模型的关键区别在于：1）后者表现得像智能体，2）后者产生幻觉更少。但这和规划无关（要产生幻觉你仍然需要规划）。这更多是因为后基础训练专门是在为那些不是幻觉的东西提供正奖励。改变 RL 期间奖励函数的计算方式并不会产生规划，它只是让模型倾向于生成更像 RL 目标的回复。Karpathy 有一个很好的入门视频讲这个。[VIDEO] 总的来说，这种吹毛求疵显得很奇怪。是的，从机械层面讲，使用模型仍然是“给定这个上下文，下一个 token 是什么”。不，这并不意味着它们不做规划，或者对其回复的整体结构没有更高层次的视角，或者诸如此类。
comments.text: > The models still _generate_ response token-by-token, but they pick tokens _not_ based on tokens that maximize probabilities at each token. This is also not how base training works. In base training the loss is chosen given a context, which can be gigantic. It's never about just the previous token, it's about a whole response in context. The context could be an entire poem, a play, a worked solution to a programming problem, etc, etc. So you would expect to see the same type of (apparent) higher-level planning from base trained models and indeed you do and can easily verify this by downloading a base model from HF or similar and prompting it to complete a poem. The key differences between base and agentic models are 1) the latter behave like agents, and 2) the latter hallucinate less. But that isn't about planning (you still need planning to hallucinate something). It's more to do with post-base training specifically being about providing positive rewards for things which aren't hallucinations. Changing the way the reward function is computed during RL doesn't produce planning, it simply inclines to model to produce responses that are more like the RL targets. Karpathy has a good intro video on this. [VIDEO] In general the nitpicking seems weird. Yes, on a mechanical level, using a model is still about "given this context, what is the next token". No, that doesn't mean that they don't plan, or have higher-level views of the overal structure of their response, or whatever.

comments.author: insin
comments.story_title: AI LLMs can't count lines in a file
comments.why_zh: 解释了 LLM 如何工作，因此数行数会失败。
comments.text_zh: 考虑到它们的工作方式，你为什么会期望它们能做到呢？[1] 我工作的地方有个人想用 LLM 来评估一个内部多项选择题测验的作答（A、B 或 C），根据答对总数的组合以及是否答对了特定问题，把人分到不同的桶里。他们花了一周时间来回做“prompt engineering”，对评分应如何工作的指令做了细微修改，但对准确性和一致性没有明显影响。这又是一个让我觉得某人在要求某件事时，对这件事本该怎么发生毫无机制层面理解的场景。也许一个“thinking”模型（为什么“AI”公司总是这样滥用术语？（反问））本可以把足够多的东西放进 context，从而更接近更好的结果；但我拿过他们的 prompt，让它改为写代码，结果它被转换成了一段注释过多但足够简单的代码，每次都能完美完成工作，其中还包括一条注释：他们提供的指令有一个缺口，即用某种答案组合作答的人不会落入任何桶里。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Why would you expect them to be able to given how they work? [1] Someone where I work was trying to get an LLM to evaluate responses to an internal multiple-choice quiz (A, B or C), putting people into different buckets based on a combination of the total number of correct responses and having answered specific questions correctly. They spent a week "prompt engineering" it back and forth, with subtle changes to their instructions on how the scoring should work, with no appreciable effect on accuracy or consistency. That's another scenario where I felt someone was asking for something with no mechanical sympathy for how it was supposed to happen. Maybe a "thinking" model (why do "AI" companies always abuse terms like this? (rhetorical)) would have been able to get enough stuff into the context for it to be able to get closer to a better outcome, but I took their prompt asked it to write code instead, and got it translated into some overly-commented but simple-enough code which would do the job perfectly every time, including a comment that the instructions they'd provided had a gap where people answering with a certain combination of answers wouldn't fall into any bucket. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: CamperBob2
comments.story_title: Using secondary school maths to demystify AI
comments.why_zh: Karpathy 对 transformer 中 native computation 的讨论。
comments.quote_zh: Karpathy 关于 native computation 的讨论：（从 1:46:56 开始）
comments.text_zh: “那是后训练。”不，不是。读论文。他们讨论的是上下文本身的一种涌现属性：“对于所有任务，GPT-3 都是在没有任何梯度更新或微调的情况下应用的，任务和少样本示例完全通过与模型的文本交互来指定。”我说的是像两个四位数相乘这样的任务（对推理模型来说，稳妥点说是两个八位数），美国五、六年级学生按理说都能毫无问题地做到——不用计算器。我也是。比如，看看 Karpathy 关于 native computation 的讨论：[VIDEO]（从 1:46:56 开始）。上下文中的前几个 token 实际上充当了某种通用计算的基底。我不假装自己理解这一点，它可能仍是一个开放研究话题，但它是 transformer 又一个出人意料的涌现属性。在这个阶段，你要是信任这个属性，那就太疯狂了——Karpathy 做那个视频时，如果他不想让模型对更复杂的问题瞎编解法，就得明确告诉模型“Use code”——但你要是信任一个上周才学会长除法的五年级学生的答案，那也同样疯狂。老实说，我很乐意被归到和当今最伟大物理学家同一阵营。现在可不是你躺在智力功劳簿上吃老本的好时候。Penrose 也一样。
comments.text: That's post-training No, it is not. Read the paper. They are discussing an emergent property of the context itself: "For all tasks, GPT-3 is applied without any gradient updates or fine-tuning, with tasks and few-shot demonstrations specified purely via text interaction with the model." I'm talking about tasks like multiplying two 4-digit numbers (let's say 8-digit, just to be safe, for reasoning models), which 5th or 6th graders in the US are expected to be able to do with no problem - without using a calculator. So am I. See, for example, Karpathy's discussion of native computation: [VIDEO] (starts at 1:46:56). The first few tokens in the context actually serve as some sort of substrate for general computation. I don't pretend to understand that, and it may still be something of an open research topic, but it's one more unexpected emergent property of transformers. You'd be crazy to trust that property at this stage -- at the time Karpathy was making the video, he needed to explicitly tell the model to "Use code" if he didn't want it to just make up solutions to more complex problems -- but you'd also be crazy to trust answers from a 5th-grader who just learned long division last week. Feeling quite comfortable being classed in the same camp with the greatest living physicist, honestly. Not a great time for you to rest on your intellectual laurels. Same goes for Penrose.
